source: បច្ចេកទេស ដាំដុះដំណាំដំឡូងជ្វា (Sweet Potato Cultivation Techniques), MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, 2018
text:
Planting depth depends on soil type: in sandy soil, cuttings can be planted with about 2 nodes buried; in heavier clay-type soil, only 1 node should be buried, as this produces better establishment in that soil type.

Plant spacing is typically 30-50cm between plants within a row, with row spacing (ridge-to-ridge) of about 1 meter. Ridges/beds should be worked to a fine tilth, breaking up large soil clods (larger than roughly 4-5cm) before planting, and 1-2 vine cuttings are typically planted per hole/position.
caveat: Spacing and clod-size figures are transcribed from a scanned page with some legibility limitations; treat as approximate. See also the duplicate-check caveat on Source C's overview file.
